newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran protesters call German embassy "2nd spy den".
newsitem.headline: Iran protesters call German embassy "2nd spy den".

text.p: Hardline Islamic demonstrators rallied outside the German embassy in Tehran on Tuesday in a third protest against German accusations that Iran ordered the killings of Kurdish dissidents in Berlin.

About 1,OOO members of Ansar-e Hizbollah (Supporters of the Party of God) chanted "This is the second den of spies" -- a reference to the United States embassy which was seized by radical Islamic students in 1979.
Dozens of riot police protected the embassy and protesters were kept behind a fence set up in the middle of the street.

"We are here to commemorate the martyrs of Iraqi chemical weapons that were made with German help," a rally organiser said over a loudspeaker. The crowd responded by chanting: "Death to fascist Germany, Death to pro-American Germany."
Some demonstrators carried large colour photographs, some close-ups, of bodies of victims of chemical weapons.
The protesters demanded a formal apology from Germany and chanted "The incompetent ambassador should be expelled."
The embassy was closed and callers were told normal business would resume on Wednesday.
In Bonn, a German government spokesman on Monday rejected allegations by Iranian officials and media that Germany had delivered missiles and chemical weapons to Iraq during the 1980-88 Iran-Iraq war.

This was the third protest rally at the embassy since a German prosecutor last week accused Iran's supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and other Tehran officials of ordering the 1992 killing of three Kurdish opposition leaders and their translator at a Berlin restaurant.
Iran's top judge on Monday asked Germany to end the row by withdrawing the charges.

"We would like German leaders to take a correct and principled position...Until German leaders announce their official position, we are assuming this problem to have been caused by an inexperienced and error-prone prosecutor," head of judiciary Ayatollah Mohammad Yazdi said.

The row threatens ties between Iran and its main trade partner. Also at risk is the European Union's "critical dialogue" with Iran which Bonn has promoted as an alternative to U.S. sanctions aimed at isolating the Islamic republic.

Tehran has repeatedly denied any role in the killings and officially protested on Thursday to Bonn over the charges. Germany prosecutors have demanded life sentences against an Iranian and a Lebanese who were tried for the killings.
